  a. ITEM:
  601-611 North Brand Boulevard
  PDR 1916682

  PROJECT DESCRIPTION
  To construct a new 852-room hotel on the surface parking lot area fronting Sanchez Drive,
  while maintaining the existing 14-story office building fronting Brand Boulevard, the one-
  story gym building on the southeast corner of Brand Boulevard and Doran Street, and the
  five-story parking garage fronting Doran Street (all existing buildings/structures built in
  1972), on the 5.2 acre project site located in the DSP-Gateway District. The hotel will consist
  of two towers above a four-story podium. The westerly tower will be 34 stories (including the
  podium) and approximately 370 feet in height. The easterly tower will be 35 stories
  (including the podium) and approximately 380 feet in height. A total of 1,949 parking spaces
  (existing and proposed) will be located on the site, including parking required for the existing
  office and gym uses within the existing parking garage, as well as the required parking for
  the proposed hotel within the new development. The Board will be performing an advisory
  review for the City Council Stage I preliminary review.

  ENVIRONMENTAL DETERMINATION
  The project is being reviewed in an advisory role by the Design Review Board. The Board’s
  recommendations will be forwarded to the City Council for their Stage I review of the project.
  Environmental review for the project will occur between the Stage I and Stage II review of
  the project by the City Council.

MINUTES
  REGULAR MEETING OF THE DESIGN REVIEW BOARD MEETING
  COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT DEPARTMENT
  CITY OF GLENDALE, CA

  Thursday, October 22, 2020

Due to the evolving situation with the COVID-19 novel coronavirus and health recommendations from
the LA County Health Department regarding social distancing, the Design Review Meeting was
available to the public online and electronically. Board members and the general public participated in
the meeting from the safety of their homes.

DRB Meeting called to order at 5:10 p.m.

1. ROLL CALL: Present: Minas (via Webex), Chair Simonian (physically present in the
  Council Chamber), Smith (via Webex), Welch (via Webex)

  Community Development Department Staff – Jay Platt, Vilia Zemaitaitis, Roger Kiesel (all
  three present in the Council Chamber

  bulletin board outside City Hall.

3. APPROVAL OF MINUTES:

7. NEW BUSINESS:
  a. 601-611 North Brand Blvd.
  DRB Case No. PDR 1729272

  Speaking on the item:
  Mark Spector (Applicant)
  Salim Narayanan (Architect)

8. COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT DEPARTMENT UPDATES
  a. Upcoming Amendments to Title 30 of the Glendale Municipal Code, 1995,
  regarding Design Review for Projects in the DSP, Murals, Rebuilds Following
  Natural Disaster, and Related Updates
    DESIGN REVIEW BOARD
  Advisory Review and Comments

Meeting Date  October 22, 2020  DRB Case No.  PDR Case No.1916682

  Address  601-611 N. Brand Blvd.

  Applicant  ONNI Group

Project Summary:

The proposal consists of a new hotel containing 852 guest rooms in two towers to be built on a
surface parking lot at the north edge of a 5.2 acre site bounded by the west side of Brand
Boulevard, the south side of Sanchez Drive, and the north side of Doran Street. The existing
14-story office building and one-story gym building (which both also front Brand Blvd.), and the
five-story parking garage (fronting Doran Street) will be retained. The hotel will consist of a
four-story podium with two towers. The west tower will be 34 stories and approximately 370
feet in height. The east tower will be 35 stories and approximately 380 feet in height. The 852
rooms feature a high percentage of large suites and rooms (e.g. 8 at 2059 SF; 16 at 1334-
1380 SF; 248 at 1005-1077 SF; with the balance ranging from about 500 to 800 SF).

Lobby and retail areas will be located at street level along Sanchez Drive and commercial
areas located along Brand Boulevard. A landscaped roof deck is located between the two
towers. A total of 1,949 parking spaces (existing and proposed) will be located on the site,
which includes parking required for the existing office and gym uses in the existing parking
garage as well as the proposed hotel. Publicly accessible open space is concentrated in the
eastern portion of the site and includes an existing plaza and walkways in the southeastern
portion of the site as well as plazas in the northeastern portion of the site proposed as part of
the project.

Design Review Board:

  Board Member  Present  Absent
  Minas  X
  Simonian  X
  Smith  X
  Welch  X

DRB Comments and Questions:

Site Planning
  •  Publicly accessible open space.
  o The proposed publicly accessible open space should be better designed and
  integrated with the existing open space. The Board believes existing open space
   that is not being touched by the project should not be included toward the open
  space that the applicant is providing.
  o  The outdoor common areas need to integrate the ability of restaurants to have
  outdoor dining areas.
  o  Concern voiced regarding the connectivity of the various areas of open space.
  o  Current proposal should address the use and vision of the plaza at the Brand and
  Sanchez intersection.
  o  The publicly accessible open space plaza along Brand Boulevard is divided by the
  driveway into the project. Consider eliminating or relocated the driveway to allow for
  one uninterrupted space.
  o  Will the existing publicly accessible open space be improved? Consider/clarify new
  paving, landscaping or seating.
  o  Use of the existing, internal paseo (in the southern portion of the site) as publicly
  accessible open space is not in the spirit of the Downtown Specific Plan.

  •  Other open space.
  o Clarify the programming of the proposed indoor and outdoor amenity spaces on the
  podium (Fifth level) of the project.
  o Consideration should be given to providing roof decks at the top of the towers.

  •  Circulation.
  o Consideration should be given to how deliveries/Uber/other services and traffic
  utilize the site and parking area,
  o Concern raised by the Board regarding traffic circulation to and from the project from
  Sanchez Drive, as well as internal vehicular and pedestrian circulation within the
  garage of the project.

Mass and Scale
  •  Scale of project is overly excessive, especially in light of the sizes of the hotel rooms.
  Consequently, the size and height of the project is excessive, as well.
  •  The massing of the towers does not address the existing site context and the towers do
  not step down to adjacent buildings.
  •  The project features appropriate articulation/modulation, but not enough to make up for
  or alleviate the excessive size of the project. Bay articulation should be enhanced.
  •  The Board commented that many hotel rooms have recently come on-line in the City
  and questioned the need for an 800-room hotel, and especially the large sizes of hotel
  rooms in relation to typical hotel layouts, though this is not germane to design review.
  •  The Board had concern regarding the additional height and FAR granted to the hotel
  use as part of the community benefit incentive program, particularly in light of the
  proposed room sizes. The number of hotel rooms also results in a larger parking
  requirement, and consequently (in combination with the room sizes) further increases
  the FAR for the project to the maximum allowed in the DSP Gateway District.
  •  There was a concern regarding the ability of the project to meet fire/life safety
  regulations, which are not germane to design review but will be addressed as the
  project moves forward.
 Design and Detailing
  •  Overall, the design detailing of the project is well thought out, the modern design is
  fresh, and the renderings are well-done. However, the design is too “urban” for
  Glendale and is not specific to the City. The project could be located anywhere.
  •  The Board remarked that the corners of the towers as being well-designed and the
  “wave-like” façade is attractive yet the repetition of materials and volumes makes the
  building look busy.
  •  Concern noted with how the design of the building will “weather” and age over time.
  •  Ambiguous wording to describe building finishes needs to be more specific for Stage II
  review.
  •  The project is a campus and entire city block. The applicant is not proposing any
  changes to the existing building facades. Some consideration should be made to
  façade improvements to the existing on-site buildings to integrate these buildings into
  the proposed project.

DRB Staff Member  Roger Kiesel, AICP, Senior Planner
